items.title: 43,000 residents made record number of visits to food banks in Mississauga: report
items.summary: Some 43,000 residents used Food Banks Mississauga’s vast network of agencies and food programs more than 513,000 times in the past year in what the organization says is a record number of visits in its 40-year history. ” Prior to the latest record-breaking number, nearly 49,000 people in need made more than 503,000 visits to FBM’s network the previous year, which marked a 20 per cent rise from the 12-month period before that. Food Banks Mississauga’s 2026 Thanksgiving Drive, which runs until Oct. 16, aims to raise $900,000. ” Food Banks Mississauga CEO Meghan Nicholls said she hopes the city, as it usually does, thinks about those in need. “Thanksgiving is meant to be a time of abundance, centred around food. As we prepare to gather with our loved ones, tables overflowing with food, we can’t forget about our neighbours who won’t be able to do the same,” Nicholls said in a news release on Thursday. “Someone walks through the doors of one of our food programs every 22 seconds they are open. This year marks our 40th anniversary. Food banks began as temporary ’emergency rooms’ and have now become necessary ‘family doctors’ due to a lack of systemic support. “As our provincial and federal governments prioritize cross-border economic concerns, we can’t lose sight of those in our own community who are most at risk,” she continued.

items.title: Can’t leave home? This little-known Mississauga voting option can help
items.summary: For some Mississauga residents, getting to a polling station for the municipal election isn’t simply inconvenient; it may be impossible. A new City of Mississauga pilot project is offering a solution by bringing the voting process directly to the homes of some residents who are unable to leave because of illness, injury or mobility limitations. The Vote From Front Door program is being offered for the 2026 municipal election and is intended for eligible voters who cannot leave their homes and who also cannot appoint someone else to cast a ballot for them as a proxy. The program could be an important option for residents who might otherwise be unable to participate in the Oct. 26 election, although the number of appointments available through the pilot is limited. Ward 6 Councillor Joe Horneck has been promoting the program and says residents should have an opportunity to exercise their right to vote even when health or mobility issues prevent them from getting to a voting location. Under the program, voting will take place by appointment before election day. A trained team of two or three election officials will visit the voter’s home and facilitate the process. The visit isn’t simply a matter of handing someone a ballot at the front door. The city says the same principles surrounding privacy and the integrity of the vote at a regular voting location will apply during a Vote From Front Door appointment. Residents must first register through the City of Mississauga Elections Office. Registration does not guarantee a home voting appointment, as the Elections Office will determine whether each applicant meets the program’s requirements.

items.title: New GO station in Toronto will also improve service in Mississauga and Brampton: province
items.summary: Major construction is underway on a new GO station being built in west Toronto that’s also expected to dramatically improve public transit for riders in Mississauga, Brampton, York and elsewhere across the region. Crews working on the Woodbine GO station, located just steps from Mississauga at Woodbine Racetrack, “are now building station platforms that will connect thousands of daily riders to the Kitchener GO Line, Union Pearson Express and regional transit services across Toronto, York Region, Brampton and Mississauga,” said the provincial government, adding the latest stage of construction is “another significant milestone” in its plan to provide two-way, all-day service across core segments of the GO Transit network. ” Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who last year described a completed Woodbine station as a “game changer” for commuters, said on Thursday latest progress on the new GO depot “is great news for families and commuters in Etobicoke and along the entire Kitchener Line,” which also runs through Toronto, Mississauga (Malton GO station), Brampton, Halton Hills and Guelph among other municipalities. “As part of our historic expansion of GO service across the Greater Golden Horseshoe, this new station will increase capacity, cut travel times and connect thousands more people to reliable, affordable transit,” Ford added. When completed at a yet-to-be-determined date, Woodbine GO station will include island platforms serving GO Transit and UP Express trains, a bus loop connecting riders to local transit, dedicated GO parking, pedestrian bridges and fully accessible, barrier-free facilities, the province said in a news release. In addition to Woodbine Racetrack, the station will create new links between the UP Express, Kitchener GO train and Toronto Pearson Airport, as well as local bus services including the TTC, MiWay, York Region Transit and Brampton Transit, the Ontario government added.

items.title: 71 vehicles broken into in Mississauga; man faces dozens of charges
items.summary: A man faces dozens of charges after 71 vehicles were broken into in Mississauga earlier this month, resulting in “significant property damage and financial losses for residents,” police say. “The incidents occurred during the early morning hours of Sept. 3 and Sept. 6, and targeted neighbourhoods throughout Mississauga,” Peel Regional Police said on Thursday. Investigators said the nearly six dozen vehicles were targeted by a culprit who either smashed car windows or entered through unlocked doors before stealing valuables. “While no vehicles were stolen and all vehicles were unoccupied at the time, the incidents resulted in significant property damage and financial losses for residents,” police said in a news release. items.title: Beat the lines on Election Day. Vote in the Advance Polls
items.summary: Voters can get an early start on Mississauga’s 2026 Municipal Election with advance voting taking place from October 6 to 11. The City of Mississauga encourages eligible voters to take advantage of advance voting on Election Day, Monday, October 26. Advance voting gives voters more days and more locations to cast their ballot before Election Day. It is the same voting process, offered earlier, so you can choose a time that works best for you. Advance voting helps make voting easier, reduces lineups and gives voters more flexibility. If you have work, school, caregiving responsibilities, travel plans or other commitments on October 26, advance voting can help you make a plan and have your say. Vote in advance from Tuesday, October 6 to Sunday, October 11. ) on October 6 and 7. From October 8 to 11, locations will be open across the city, and you can vote at any advance voting location. On Election Day, eligible voters may vote at a voting location in the ward in which they live or have property. You will elect the Mayor, Ward/Regional Councillor and School Board Trustees. Bring your Voter notification card (if you receive one) and one piece of acceptable identification. Before you vote, take a few minutes to make sure you are eligible, your voter information is correct and you know where you can cast your ballot. This helps make the voting process faster and helps election staff give you the right ballot.

items.title: Don’t let water quality go down the drain this pool season
items.summary: Getting ready to close your outdoor pool? A few simple steps can help keep chemicals out of the stormwater system and protect Lake Ontario, the source of Mississauga's drinking water. Many Mississauga homes have backyard pools that need to be drained and winterized before colder weather arrives. If you’re closing your outdoor pool for the winter, it’s important to do it safely and responsibly. Prevent pool chemicals from entering waterways and harming wildlife by disposing of them the right way. This helps protect your health and our environment. Remove leaves, grass and other debris from the water. This helps keep the water cleaner over the winter. If you have an automatic pool cleaner, remove it, drain it, let it dry and store it until next season. Test the pool water for chlorine and pH levels. 0, which is neutral. After treatment, do not add any more chemicals or algae-control products for at least seven days. Before draining any water, make sure the chlorine level is zero. Pool and spa owners must follow the City of Mississauga’s by-law when draining water.
